<description>
{
 "summary": "Fixes a transaction relay liveness hole in TxOrphanage by reassigning an orphan scheduled for reconsideration to another remaining announcer when the assigned announcer's announcement is erased upon disconnect or eviction. It also adds an end-to-end P2P fuzz harness (p2p_1p1c_liveness) driving real message processing and validation to verify 1p1c relay invariants against adversarial peer behaviors, alongside unit and fuzz test updates.",
 "problem": "When a missing parent transaction is accepted, child orphans are scheduled in a single randomly chosen announcer's work set for reconsideration. If that announcer disconnects or is evicted before the orphan is retried, the orphan is abandoned in the orphanage without being re-evaluated, and re-announcements from other peers are ignored because the transaction is already stored, allowing peers to intentionally delay transactions like CPFP children until eviction.",
 "evidence": [
  "PR description: 'With that flag turned off, the target finds this bug on master from an empty corpus in under an hour on one core; an earlier version found it first (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36371#issuecomment-5937814761).'",
  "Commit e974d21b4e: 'If that announcer disconnects or is evicted first, the orphan is never retried, and re-announcements by the other announcers don't fetch it again since it is already held. This keeps e.g. a CPFP child of a parent that pays for itself out of the mempool until the orphan is evicted, and an announcer can cause it on purpose.'"
 ],

<category name="tests" title="Test infrastructure">
## Covers

The machinery of testing rather than tests of a particular area: the
functional test framework and runner, unit test utilities, the fuzzing
harnesses and corpora, benchmarks, linters, sanitizer configuration,
and fixes for flaky tests whose cause is in the framework. A test that
pins the behavior of one area (a wallet migration test, a p2p relay
test) belongs to that area, not here. The Tests and Fuzzing labels are
a prior, but a labeled PR whose tests are about one area goes to that
area instead.

## What matters here

Signal first: fixes for flaky or misleading tests, since a red CI that
nobody trusts hides real failures. Then coverage of high-risk code paths
that the fuzzers or functional tests do not reach, especially
consensus, mempool policy, and p2p message handling. Then framework
capabilities that unblock tests other areas need. Then test speed, which
every contributor pays for on every run. Then cleanliness of the test
code.

Adding tests for their own sake ranks low; adding a test that catches a
realistic regression ranks high.
